subject: RFI: Deployment partitioning and threat summary for BlueCrest Bank
messages:
From: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@bluecrestbank.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluecrestbank.com>, Eve Shaw <eve.shaw@security-consult.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: Network isolation & threat modelling deliverables (BlueCrest RFP)

Camila,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Our security & architecture review requires a set of documents we need by EOD next Monday (2026-07-26): a network diagram showing customer-isolated deployment options, a matrix that maps isolation controls to threat vectors, and a brief threat-model summary covering delegated key management, cross-tenant attack paths, and admin plane exposure. We've attached the RFP section (pdf) for reference.

A couple of clarifying asks up front:
- Can you indicate which parts of the runtime are multi-tenant vs single-tenant in the hosted offering?
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, please call out every network boundary and where TLS/mTLS is enforced.
- We need a redacted version suitable to share with our third-party assessor (no customer-specific telemetry).

Eve from Security-Consult is looping in for specialist review. If you need additional detail on our environment (VPC ranges, on-prem connectors) I can send a short inventory.

Regards,
Daniel
Head of Platform Security
BlueCrest Bank

Attachment: BlueCrest_RFP_Section6_Security.pdf

Subject: Re: RFI: Network isolation & threat modelling deliverables (BlueCrest RFP)

Daniel — thanks for the clear asks. We can assemble the requested artifacts and deliver a redacted set for your assessor. Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:

1) "Multi-tenant vs single-tenant" — do you want a per-component mapping (e.g., control plane, model serving, control plane datastore) or a high-level table? We can do both but want to confirm level of detail.
2) Redaction: we'll remove telemetry and example request payloads; is there any PII in your sample inventory we should be specifically aware of?

Plan: I'll coordinate with Solutions (Laura) to produce the diagram + matrix and with Legal (Stephanie) on redaction language. Ben, please review the threat summary draft and approve inclusion of our SOC+CCPA summary extract.

I'll target a first pass by Monday 09:00 AM ET and a final redacted bundle by EOD Monday. If that timing doesn't work, tell me and we'll adjust.

—Camila

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Draft: BlueCrest RFI artifacts (network diagram + partitioning matrix)

Camila / team — attaching the first-pass artifacts. Highlights and callouts below; attachments: bluecrest_network_diagram_v2.png (diagram with layers), deployment_partitioning_matrix.xlsx (controls->threat mapping), redacted_threat_summary_2026-07.pdf (3 pages, high-level).

Key summaries (TL;DR):
- Hosted (Redwood API): control plane (authn/tenant routing) is multi-tenant; model execution occurs on tenant-isolated worker pools logically separated by namespace and tokenized KV caches. Network boundary: public API ingress -> customer-specific routing -> worker pool VPC namespace. TLS is enforced end-to-end (client->edge TLS, edge->worker mTLS).
- Dedicated: fully single-tenant GPU pools with private subnets; management/control plane traffic uses a dedicated management VPC with strict IP allowlists and mutual TLS for operator APIs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed networking; our control plane can be deployed in a customer VPC or we provide an offline on-prem bundle. All data plane egress policies are explicit and configurable; we provide blocking egress rules and optional firewall templates.

Threat-model mapping (high level):
- Cross-tenant data exfiltration: mitigations include strict namespace isolation, KV cache scoping, token-scoped KMS keys, and runtime sandboxing (process-level limits).
- Admin-plane compromise: mitigations include role-separation (operator vs SRE), MFA + hardware token enforcement on management plane accounts, and dedicated management VPC for Dedicated customers.
- Lateral movement from customer-managed connectors: recommend network ACLs, ephemeral credentials for connectors, and egress rule templates.

Notes on keys and telemetry: we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments. When CMK is used, key access policies are scoped to a tenant ID and rotated per-customer; redacted_threat_summary includes rotation cadence and signing domain recommendations.

Attachment summaries are embedded in the pdf cover page. Laura

Attachment: bluecrest_network_diagram_v2.png (1.2MB), deployment_partitioning_matrix.xlsx (120KB), redacted_threat_summary_2026-07.pdf (85KB)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Draft: BlueCrest RFI artifacts (network diagram + partitioning matrix)

Camila — quick thumbs up on Laura's draft. A couple of tactical edits before sending to BlueCrest:
- Add explicit statement that in Hosted the persistence layer for transient request telemetry is sampled and retained only for troubleshooting; include retention window.
- For Dedicated, add note about optional private peering and whether we can accept customer-provided BGP routes (we can, with our netops team, under SLA).

Also recommend we include an excerpt from our SOC2 report (redacted) and the summary page from our penetration test (high level findings only). Stephanie, can Legal sign off on that redacted bundle?

Ben Carter
VP, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: BlueCrest RFI bundle: network partitioning + threat summary (redacted)

Daniel / team — attaching the redacted bundle for your assessor. Included items: 1) bluecrest_network_diagram_v2.png — labelled for Hosted / Dedicated / Private boundaries, 2) deployment_partitioning_matrix.xlsx — maps controls to threat vectors and recommended mitigations, 3) redacted_threat_summary_2026-07.pdf — three-page narrative with key mitigations and KMS guidance, 4) SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf (excerpt), 5) pentest_summary_highlevel.pdf (excerpt).

Highlights:
- Hosted: end-to-end TLS + mTLS between edge and worker pools; tenant scoping enforced in runtime and KMS scoping for keys; telemetry is sampled and retained for up to 30 days for troubleshooting (configurable under Dedicated/Private plans).
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools with dedicated management VPC and optional private peering; operator access limited via bastion + hardware MFA and IP allowlists.
- Private: control plane can be delivered under customer control; BYOK supported via HSM/KMS integrations.

Eve — as requested, the bundle is redacted but includes the technical claims you need for assessment. Please advise if additional redactions are required.

Next steps: Please confirm receipt. If everything looks good, we can produce a DocuSign-ready statement of shared responsibilities and a one-week technical follow-up session with our NetOps + Security engineers.

Thanks,
